hints: Focus on the H-X bond itself, since both oxidation and thermal decomposition of hydrogen halides involve breaking that bond.
Remember that $\text{HI}$ is a strong reducing agent that is easily oxidised to iodine, while $\text{HF}$ and $\text{HCl}$ are not oxidised by concentrated sulfuric acid.
Connect both trends to bond enthalpy, which falls from HF to HI as the atoms get larger, making the molecule both easier to break by heat and easier to oxidise.
walkthrough:
**Recall how H-X bond strength changes**

Think of going from HF down to HI. The halogen atom gets much larger, so orbital overlap gets poorer and the bond gets longer and weaker.

Bond enthalpy trend:
$$\text{H-F} > \text{H-Cl} > \text{H-Br} > \text{H-I}$$

**Apply this to thermal stability**

Thermal decomposition needs heat to break the H-X bond. A weaker bond needs less heat, so stability decreases down the group.

General idea:
$$2\text{HX} \rightarrow \text{H}_2 + \text{X}_2$$
$\text{HF}$ is very stable, $\text{HI}$ decomposes most easily on heating.

**Apply this to ease of oxidation**

Oxidation of $\text{HX}$ means the halide ion $\text{X}^-$ loses electrons to form $\text{X}_2$. Larger ions hold their outer electrons less tightly and lose them more easily.

So $\text{I}^-$ is oxidised most easily, $\text{F}^-$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ are hardest. Ease of oxidation increases, in other words it gets easier to oxidise down the group.

**Match both trends to the table**

We need easier to oxidise down the group plus thermal stability decreases down the group. That combination matches only one row.

options.A: Half right and half wrong. It is easier to oxidise down the group, but thermal stability does not increase. Stronger bonding is at the top with HF, not at the bottom with HI.
options.B: Both parts are wrong. Halides do not get harder to oxidise down the group, iodide is actually the best reducing agent. Stability also does not increase, the H-X bond gets weaker.
options.C: Correct on both counts. Weaker H-X bonds down the group mean less energy is needed to break them by heating, so thermal stability decreases, and larger halide ions lose electrons more readily, so oxidation gets easier from HF to HI.
options.D: Half right and half wrong. Thermal stability does decrease down the group, but oxidation does not get more difficult. Students sometimes confuse oxidising power of halogens (which decreases down the group) with reducing power of halides (which increases down the group).
